title: Inheritance and Constructors 1

lines.explanation:
The Container class creates a constructor which asks for an int parameter. This 
means that for creating a Container object, we need to specify the capacity. 
Thus, the null constructor Container() is "deactivate" in the class : we can not 
create Container objects by doing just "new Container()", we need to specify the 
capacity.

the operator this refers to the object which is being built. In this case is used to 
differentiate the capacity attribute of the object (this.capacity) from the 
parameter 
capacity of the constructor (avoid to write something like capacity = capacity.)
PaperBox class is a subclass of Container
This is the constructor of the class.

Since the super class Container does not have a null constructor, we need to 
explicitly call its constructor, using the reference super(). Here super() refers to 
the 
constructor Container(int capacity) in class Container.

GallonPlasticBottle class is a subclass of Container and is aimed to create objects 
representing plastic bottles of 1 gallon capacity
This is the constructor of the class.

Here we need to call the super class constructor, and since GallonPlasticBottle will 
define objects of 1 gallon capacity, the value 1 is passed
